blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Good HR teams rely on data. Every month, they look at a dashboard with the main people metrics and decide what to do next. Typical HR KPIs include voluntary turnover, time to hire, cost per hire, the employee engagement score and the internal promotion rate.

Each number tells part of the story, and together they give a clearer picture of how the company treats its people. One metric on its own can be misleading; the value comes from reading them side by side and following the trend over time.

The hardest part is not producing the numbers — it is explaining them. A good HR business partner knows how to turn a spreadsheet into a conversation with the leadership team. Collecting the data is only the beginning; the real skill is making it mean something.

items.q: According to the text, what do good HR teams do every month?
options: Look at a dashboard of the main people metrics
items.why: "Every month, they look at a dashboard with the main people metrics and decide what to do next."

items.q: Which of these is listed as a typical HR KPI?
items.why: "Typical HR KPIs include voluntary turnover, time to hire, cost per hire…"

items.q: According to the text, what is the hardest part of the job?
items.why: "The hardest part is not producing the numbers — it is explaining them."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A single number is enough to judge how a company treats its people.
Trends matter more than a snapshot.
Data only has value once it is explained.
One metric on its own can be misleading.
items.why: Inferência: o texto insiste que os números só fazem sentido em conjunto e ao longo do tempo, não isolados.

items.q: The phrase "turn a spreadsheet into a conversation" suggests that the author values…
options: communicating the meaning behind the data
keeping the numbers away from leadership
items.why: Inferência: transformar planilha em conversa é comunicar o significado, não apenas mostrar dados.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry apresentar o dashboard de RH do trimestre. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thanks, everyone. Let me take you through the quarterly HR dashboard. The headline is genuinely good: voluntary turnover is down from fourteen percent to eleven, which is now below the industry average. Fewer people are choosing to leave, and that saves us a lot in cost per hire.

But there is one number I want us to sit with. Time to hire has gone the other way — it has climbed from thirty-one days to forty-two. So we are keeping people, but we are getting slower at bringing new ones in. If you only glanced at turnover, you would think everything is fine.

Now, before anyone panics, I've drilled down into the data. Most of that delay sits in two senior roles where we chose to wait for the right candidate rather than settle. That is a deliberate trade-off, not a broken process.

My recommendation is simple: let's benchmark time to hire by seniority next quarter, instead of using one average for everyone. The trend matters more than the single figure. I'll share the full breakdown after the call.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is the good news Harry starts with?
options: Voluntary turnover is down and below the industry average
The engagement score reached a record high
items.why: "voluntary turnover is down from fourteen percent to eleven, which is now below the industry average."

items.q: What happened to time to hire?
options: It climbed from thirty-one to forty-two days
It was not measured this quarter
It stayed the same at thirty-one days
items.why: "it has climbed from thirty-one days to forty-two."

items.q: According to Harry, where does most of the delay come from?
options: Two senior roles where they waited for the right candidate
A hiring freeze imposed by finance
items.why: "Most of that delay sits in two senior roles where we chose to wait for the right candidate rather than settle."

items.q: Why does Harry say "If you only glanced at turnover, you would think everything is fine"?
options: Because leadership never reads the reports
Because a single positive metric can hide a problem elsewhere
Because turnover is the only metric that matters
items.why: Inferência: ele mostra que olhar só um número esconde o problema no tempo de contratação.

items.q: What does Harry's approach to the data suggest about him?
options: He wants to speed up hiring at any cost
He prefers to hide bad numbers from leadership
He trusts one average over any detail
He reads metrics in context and looks for the real cause
items.why: Inferência: ele detalha (drill down), separa por senioridade e valoriza a tendência — leitura em contexto.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The dashboard shows every people metric on a single screen." A dashboard is…
options: a visual summary of key metrics
items.why: Dashboard = painel: um resumo visual dos principais indicadores.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "When good people quit on their own, we call it ___."
items.why: Voluntary turnover = rotatividade voluntária: quando o colaborador escolhe sair.

items.q: "Engagement is one of the most important trends to watch." A trend is…
options: a general direction of change over time
items.why: Trend = tendência: a direção da mudança ao longo do tempo, não um número isolado.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We ___ our numbers against the ___ to see if we are ahead or behind."
items.why: To benchmark = comparar; industry average = média do setor. Comparamos nossos números com a média do mercado.

items.q: "The best HR teams drill down into the data." To drill down means to…
options: examine the detail behind a number
look at the surface figure only
items.why: To drill down = detalhar / aprofundar: ir além do número de superfície para achar a causa.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem quando se apresentam dados e KPIs. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Leadership still has to sign off on the new hiring budget." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new dashboard to all regions next quarter." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, região por região.

items.q: "Two managers pushed back on the new turnover target." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Better onboarding could really move the needle on engagement." This means it could…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.

items.q: "Let's not read too much into a single month of data." To read too much into something means to…
options: give it more meaning than it deserves
items.why: Read too much into = tirar conclusões exageradas de algo pequeno, como um único mês.
